{{Quote|He's ridiculous&hellip;a guy no one's ever liked or trusted&hellip;and one of the worst enemies I ever had.|Lando Calrissian|<ref name="msw99" />}}
'''Barpotomous Drebble''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] businessman who had a weakness for [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] and a furious temper. The owner of a [[Barpotomous Drebble's tavern|tavern]] on the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|Hunter's]] [[Planet/Legends|World]] of [[Keyorin]], Drebble accumulated enough wealth to live comfortably. At some point, Drebble came into contact with [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], an accomplished [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] and skilled gambler. The encounter ended poorly for Drebble, and he swore vengeance on Calrissian. Drebble clashed with Calrissian several times over the following [[Standard year/Legends|years]], including an attempt to interfere in Calrissian's [[Sabacc/Legends|card game]] with the [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]] of [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], [[Dominic Raynor]]. Drebble's meddling indirectly resulted in Calrissian winning control of the Cloud [[City/Legends|City]] resort from Raynor. In another encounter, Drebble nearly captured Calrissian and his friend, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], on the planet [[Stenos/Legends|Stenos]], but Drebble's employees were unable to prevent the two from escaping.

Calrissian, for his part, decided to get back at Drebble by using his name as an alias whenever he was involved in a dangerous mission for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]]. Calrissian hoped that this gesture would lead any potential enemies encountered on these missions back to his nemesis; however, Calrissian's actions while masquerading as "Drebble" had the opposite effect, causing the Alliance to seek out Calrissian's nemesis and commend him for his bravery. As a result, a short [[Time/Legends|time]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], a confused Drebble found himself promoted to [[Captain/Legends|captain]] and declared a hero of the Alliance to Restore the Republic. Drebble's newfound status as a hero led him to a leadership position on the planet Stenos. He controlled a substantial section of the [[Capital City (Stenos)|Stenos capital]] and ruled it in the best interests of the [[Alliance of Free Planets]], the interim government that preceded the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].

==Biography==
===Card shark===
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Barpotomous<ref name="ll">{{Tales|3|Lady Luck (comic story)}}</ref> Drebble's success as a businessman came from the [[Barpotomous Drebble's tavern|large tavern]] on [[Keyorin]], which he owned and operated. The [[Planet/Legends|planet]] was a haven for [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], and Drebble's place was a popular hangout on the Hunter's World.<ref name="msw85" /> However, Drebble's success did not mean that he spent all his [[Time/Legends|time]] on Keyorin. Drebble was known to frequent the popular [[Cloud City Casino]] in pursuit of entertainment and wealth.<ref name="ll" />

[[File:Drebble_2.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lando Calrissian raises the stakes.]]
While still on his [[Barpotomous Drebble's homeworld|homeworld]], Drebble became familiar with the [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]. During their first encounter, there was a dispute, and Drebble would later claim that Calrissian had cheated him.<ref name="msw85" /> Sometime later, Drebble became reacquainted with Calrissian at the [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] [[Casino/Legends|Casino]]. Calrissian was an accomplished [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] player, and Drebble found himself losing a great deal to Calrissian's skills. Drebble's pride could not accept that Calrissian was a better player, and thus Drebble was convinced that Calrissian had been cheating during their games. Drebble eventually found a chance to get back at Calrissian for all his humiliating defeats.<ref name="ll" />

Calrissian found himself in a high stakes game of sabacc against [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]] [[Dominic Raynor]], and Drebble seized his chance. He bribed the dealer into sneaking a [[Skifter/Legends|skifter]], a rigged sabacc card, into the deck, throwing the game and allowing Raynor a substantial victory; Raynor's earnings took the form of Calrissian's prized [[Starship/Legends|starship]], the ''[[Cobra]]''. However, [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]], the chief administrative [[Aide/Legends|aide]] of the resort, discovered the skifter, and Drebble was subsequently kicked out of the casino. Drebble was therefore not around to see Calrissian's second game with Raynor in which he won the entire Cloud City resort.<ref name="ll" />

===Reunion===
{{Quote|That's right, Calrissian&mdash;the man who's buying you. The richest offworlder on this miserable heap of sand. The man who'll pay double any bribe you offer the guard&hellip; for you, and for anyone foolish enough to call you his friend.|Barpotomous Drebble|<ref name="msw72">[[Star Wars (1977) 72|''Star Wars'' (1977) 72]]</ref>}}
Over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]], Drebble's anger against Calrissian grew. Drebble enjoyed venting his frustration at his subordinates, giving speeches about how much of a cheat Calrissian was.<ref name="msw85" /> Drebble's tavern continued to bring in customers, and around [[3 ABY/Legends|3.5 ABY]], Drebble's wealth had allowed him to hire the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunters [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]] and [[IG-88C/Legends|IG-88C]] as part-time employees. Drebble still continued to travel off-world, and coincidentally, he was surprised to see Calrissian and his friend [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] frequenting a [[Stenos tavern|tavern]] on [[Stenos/Legends|Stenos]].<ref name="msw71" />

[[File:Drebble5.jpg|thumb|200px|Drebble receives a punch in the face.]]
Excited at the possibility of capturing Calrissian, Drebble cried out to the denizens of the tavern, declaring that he would pay 10,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to the one who captured the man who had cheated him. With the possibility of a small fortune on the line, the tavern erupted with [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] [[Laser/Legends|fire]]. However, Skywalker's [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|skills]] with a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] allowed the pair to escape. Drebble's frantic insistence that someone chase the rapidly departing Calrissian only resulted in a punch to the face from an irritated patron.<ref name="msw71" />

However, an ambush by Bossk and IG-88C stopped Calrissian from escaping, and he was put under close watch by Drebble's men. Drebble paid a hefty sum so that Calrissian could be [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|frozen]] in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] and brought back to his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. This plan was eventually foiled; due to further interference from Skywalker, Calrissian escaped from the [[Carbon-freezing chamber/Legends|carbon-freezing chamber]] untouched and outside of Drebble's grasp once again.<ref name="msw72" />

===Second chance===
{{Quote|Lando Calrissian! Wherever you are, I'm warning you&hellip;if it takes me the rest of my life&mdash;If I have to search every miserable planet in this entire galaxy, someday, I'm going to find you, and when I do&hellip;|Barpotomous Drebble|<ref name="msw85" />}}
After Calrissian's escape, Drebble's desire for revenge continued. Drebble was still the wealthiest man on Keyorin, and the illustrious bounty hunters Bossk and a newly reprogrammed [[IG-88A/Legends|IG-88A]],<ref name="msw85" /><ref name="NEGTC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> as well as two [[Stenax]] [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], were kept on retainer. Drebble loved to use the hunters as an audience for his soliloquies about getting revenge on Calrissian.<ref name="msw85" /> A short time following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Calrissian and his [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] associates, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], arrived on Keyorin to negotiate with the [[Tinketh Fo|Head of State]] about attending the [[First Conference of Free Peoples|first meeting]] of the [[Alliance of Free Planets]]. After Han convinced the official to attend the meeting, Calrissian, Solo, and Chewbacca frequented Drebble's tavern for a drink.<ref name="msw85" /> When the three went to pay for their drinks, Drebble had an abrupt reunion with his sworn enemy. Calrissian and company ran out the back door, and Drebble ordered his men, including Bossk and IG-88A, to capture Calrissian. The chase ended when Drebble and his Stenax employees cut the group off at Solo's ship, the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].<ref name="msw85" />

[[File:Drebble4.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Drebble vents his frustration to his subordinates.]]
Drebble and his two Stenax bodyguards [[Stun/Legends|stunned]] the group and dragged Calrissian to the Rebel's personal ship, the ''Cobra'', leaving Solo and Chewbacca to a [[Lemo and Sanda's gang|group of thugs]] led by the criminals [[Lemo]] and [[Sanda]]. Drebble planned to commandeer Calrissian's ship and bring him back to the first place that Calrissian had cheated him&mdash;Drebble's homeworld. The wealthy businessman planned to use his Stenax servants to exact a very personal revenge on Calrissian. However, as Drebble attempted to work the controls of the ''Cobra'', he inadvertently turned on the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], and a special report by Rebel leader [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] came over the network. The report announced that Drebble was to be declared a hero of the Rebellion, promoted to the rank of [[Captain/Legends|captain]], and given a decoration for bravery.<ref name="msw85" />

Unbeknownst to Drebble, during Calrissian's time in the Rebellion, Calrissian had often used Drebble's name as an alias in undercover missions to avoid attracting unwanted attention to himself.<ref name="msw75">[[Star Wars (1977) 75|''Star Wars'' (1977) 75]]</ref><ref name="msw79">[[Star Wars (1977) 79|''Star Wars'' (1977) 79]]</ref> The Alliance snapped up the reports of "Drebble's" exploits and declared him a hero. Drebble was shocked by the announcement, but he took to his new position with fervor. Knowing Calrissian was a member of the Alliance, Drebble released the man after Calrissian lied that he had been sent to Keyorin to give Drebble his commendations.<ref name="msw85" />

Immediately after this promotion, Lemo and Sanda's gang accosted Captain Drebble about the whereabouts of an expensive artifact, the [[Dancing Goddess/Legends|Dancing Goddess]]. The gang had believed that Solo and Chewbacca possessed the statue, but after interviewing them, they learned that the artifact was still with Calrissian. Armed with this information, they double-crossed Drebble and demanded that he turn over Calrissian to them or suffer the consequences. Drebble, having fully bought into his role as an Alliance hero, decided to heroically battle the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] gang and protect Calrissian. Before Drebble could attack the pirates, his former nemesis offered a plan of attack, which he immediately agreed to. On Calrissian's suggestion, he and Drebble gave themselves up to Lemo and Sanda's gang while his two Stenax bodyguards flew around behind the pirate group. At Drebble's signal, and with help from the intervention of Solo and Chewbacca, the Stenaxes attacked from the rear while IG-88A and Bossk began firing on the pirates from inside the ship. Surrounded and outgunned, Lemo and Sanda surrendered, but not before taking heavy casualties to their group. As a reward for Drebble's bravery and his newfound loyalty to the Rebellion, Calrissian presented him with the Dancing Goddess, much to Lemo and Sanda's dismay.<ref name="msw85" />

===Hero of the Rebellion===
[[File:Drebble3.jpg|thumb|200px|Barpotomous Drebble, the leader of the capital of Stenos]]
{{Quote|Drebble&hellip;Chewie and I are taking this&hellip;because we have to&hellip;but no one can take away the fact that you earned it. You've still got what it takes. Now you're a hero of the Alliance's peace as well as the war.|Lando Calrissian|<ref name="msw99" />}}
Within a short period, Drebble used his influence as a Rebel hero to become the leader of an entire section of the [[Capital City (Stenos)|Stenos capital]].<ref name="msw99" /> The people of Stenos greatly admired Drebble and did everything in their power to protect their beloved leader. By this time, Drebble had taken to wearing an elaborate military uniform complete with a [[Cape/Legends|cape]], and his hair had become white.<ref name="msw99" />

During the [[Nagai–Tof War|Nagai-Tof War]], Calrissian found himself on a mission to Stenos to reclaim the Dancing Goddess. The statue had been revealed to be part of an [[House of the Goddess|elaborate machine]] on the planet [[Godo]] that kept the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of the planet fit to support the native [[Godoan/Legends|Godoans]]. The absence of the Dancing Goddess had caused the machine to stop working, and the Godoans were slowly [[Death/Legends|dying]]. Calrissian was hesitant to take Drebble's award away from him, but the lives of an entire [[Species/Legends|species]] hung in the balance.<ref name="msw99" />

When Calrissian and Chewbacca arrived on Stenos to see Drebble, Drebble's loyal citizens misinterpreted the situation, believing Calrissian had arrived to harm their leader. They opened fire on the pair, and Calrissian and Chewbacca were forced to flee, eventually coming face to face with Drebble. Drebble recognized Calrissian and Chewbacca and brought them into [[Barpotomous Drebble's headquarters|his headquarters]]. When Calrissian asked for the statue, Drebble's notorious temper almost got the better of him, but he recognized that if he insisted on keeping it, he would no longer deserve it. Drebble allowed Calrissian to take the statue back to Godo, where it helped repair the machine and save the Godoans.<ref name="msw99" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|How wonderful it is to be loved!|Barpotomous Drebble|<ref name="msw99" />}}
[[File:DrebbleDancingGoddess-SW1977-99.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Drebble with the Dancing Goddess]]
Barpotomous Drebble was a large man who enjoyed a wealthy lifestyle that his profitable business provided him. He had a distinct sense of style and displayed a long mohawk throughout his career, even when his hair had turned white.<ref name="msw99" /> As a businessman on Keyorin, he was concerned with being as comfortable as possible, wearing simple sandals and a long purple robe adorned with a heavy [[Gold/Legends|gold]] chain. Additionally, Drebble claimed that his [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] were the most expensive that credits could buy.<ref name="msw71" /> Drebble was easily offended, and found it hard to forgive transgressions against him.<ref name="msw85" /> He also had a furious temper and often yelled when in a particularly foul mood. However, for all his character flaws, Drebble proved himself a shrewd businessman, using his tavern to set himself up as the wealthiest being on Keyorin.<ref name="msw72" />

Drebble's attitude and his general feeling toward life and the people around him abruptly changed after his appointment to captain. He left his tavern on Keyorin and took to living up to his newfound status in his new home on Stenos. He found himself more in control of his temper and took responsibility for the citizens of the Stenos [[Capital/Legends|capital]], eventually becoming leader of a large section of the city. With his optimistic outlook on life, Drebble's sense of style changed as well. He wore a full uniform complete with a cape, ammunition belt, and heavy boots.<ref name="msw99" />

Although he possessed a sense of style, Drebble was not a very apt fighter in hand-to-hand combat and was unable to earn the respect of his subordinates.<ref name="msw71" /> He was not familiar with the controls of starships, such as the ''Cobra'', being fully incapable of working the controls when he attempted to commandeer Calrissian's ship. However, Drebble could handle a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]], and he was a capable leader when confronted with violence, as seen when he attacked Lemo and Sanda's gang.<ref name="msw85" /> These characteristics were built upon after he became part of the Rebel Alliance, and those that he ruled over were fanatically loyal to him, willing to kill or capture anyone who might cause him harm.<ref name="msw99" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Drebble.jpg|thumb|200px|Drebble drinks while gambling in the Cloud City Casino.]]
Drebble was created by [[Mary Jo Duffy]] for use in [[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel's ''Star Wars'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] [[Star Wars (1977) 71|''Star Wars'' (1977) 71]] as an adversary to Lando Calrissian. He appeared in the [[Star Wars (1977) 72|following issue]], in which Calrissian escaped from Drebble's schemes. In two later issues in the [[Marvel Comics|Marvel]] comic series, [[Star Wars (1977) 75|''Star Wars'' (1977) 75]] and [[Star Wars (1977) 79|''Star Wars'' (1977) 79]], Calrissian used Drebble's name as an alias, in an effort to get Drebble into trouble. However, these efforts backfired, and in [[Star Wars (1977) 85|''Star Wars'' (1977) 85]], Drebble was declared a hero of the Rebel Alliance. This caused the character to ally himself with the Alliance of Free Planets, and during his last appearance in [[Star Wars (1977) 99|''Star Wars'' (1977) 99]], he proved himself to be a friend of Calrissian.

After the Marvel run, Drebble went unreferenced until the [[1995]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'', where he and his exploits in the Marvel comics were briefly mentioned in the entry for Lando Calrissian. Drebble did not make another appearance until [[2000]] in the short comic "[[Lady Luck (comic story)|Lady Luck]]," published in [[Star Wars Tales 3|''Star Wars Tales'' 3]]. At the time of publication, this comic was not fully within continuity, but references to the events of the comic in ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', ''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'', and the short story "[[Lando Calrissian: Idiot's Array]]" indicate that the comic is at least partially [[canon]] in the [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] continuity. Within this comic, the authors, [[Rich Handley]] and [[Darko Macan]], revealed Drebble's first name of Barpotomous. This name was also referenced in the [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry for [[IG-88B|IG-88]], but is misspelled "Barpotamus" in the Databank entry for [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]]. During the short comic, Drebble is seen drinking what looks like [[Wikipedia:Colt 45 (malt liquor)|Colt 45]] (seen to the right), a beverage once advertised by [[Billy Dee Williams]].<ref name="BillyDeeColt45">{{YouTube|video=0pK5HmuCMBM|text=Colt 45 Commercial With Billy Dee Williams|channel=UCZa8brAfmhn8MwnZMurqJxQ|name=Chrisdorph}}</ref> Drebble was mentioned again in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' in the entries for Calrissian, IG-88, and Bossk, which referenced his appearances in the Marvel run, and in the Calrissian entry, which referenced his presence in ''Lady Luck''.

In [[2008]], Rich Handley once again referenced Drebble in his [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] short story "Lando Calrissian: Idiot's Array." The same year, the character received an entry in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', once again summarizing his presence in the Marvel comics.
